name: Chabad of Lamorinda
tagline: Judaism with a smile, for every Jew in Lamorinda
description: Chabad of Lamorinda is a warm, welcoming Jewish center in Lafayette, California, serving Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda with Shabbat and holiday services, a Jewish preschool, Hebrew school, classes and community events. No membership required.

staff.name: Tzipora Labkowski
staff.role: Rebbetzin; Director of Lamorinda Jewish Preschool and Lamorinda Hebrew School

weekly.time: Sunday 8:00 AM; Monday to Friday 6:30 AM
weekly.name: Morning services (Shacharit), with the Torah reading on Monday and Thursday. Need to say Kaddish? You can.
weekly.title: Morning services (Shacharit)
weekly.about: Start the day with G-d and a warm group: Shacharit, the morning prayers, every morning at Chabad of Lamorinda. On Monday and Thursday the Torah is read. Saying Kaddish for a parent or a loved one? Come, and we will gladly help you say it. Prayer books with English are there to borrow, and someone will always show you the page. Tefillin? Ask, and we will help you put them on.

weekly.name: Weekly Torah class (English)
weekly.about: An hour of Torah in English on Sunday night: the weekly Torah portion, Jewish ideas for real life, and plenty of time for your questions. No background is needed and no Hebrew; just come as you are. A great way to end the weekend and start the week with meaning.

weekly.name: Tanya class in Hebrew, with Rebbetzin Tzipora Labkowski
weekly.about: Rebbetzin Tzipora Labkowski teaches Tanya, the classic book of Chassidic teaching by Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, in Hebrew, in a warm group at her home in Lafayette. Tanya explains the soul, how to find joy and meaning, and how to grow as a person, one step at a time. Call 925-384-7242 for the address and more details.
weekly.place: At the Rabbi's home in Lafayette. Call 925-384-7242 for the address and more details.

weekly.name: Torah class in Hebrew, with a meal
weekly.about: A Torah class in Hebrew with a meal: good food, good company and a lesson that speaks to today. Israelis and Hebrew speakers in Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda feel right at home. Come once, and you will want to come back.

weekly.name: Tanya class (English)
weekly.about: Tanya in English at midday: the classic book of Chassidic teaching by Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, explained simply, line by line, with time for discussion. It is about the soul, joy, and how to live with meaning. At the Rabbi's home in Lafayette; call 925-384-7242 for the address.
weekly.place: At the Rabbi's home in Lafayette. Call 925-384-7242 for the address.

weekly.name: Kabbalat Shabbat
weekly.about: Welcome Shabbat with song: Kabbalat Shabbat on Friday evening at Chabad of Lamorinda, timed with candle lighting each week ({kabbalat-shabbat} this week). Joyful singing, a short prayer service and a warm "Good Shabbos" for everyone. Prayer books with English are there to borrow. Would you like to stay for a Shabbat dinner with the Rabbi's family? Let us know.

weekly.name: Shabbat services and Kiddush lunch
weekly.about: Shabbat morning services from 10 AM to 12 PM: traditional, joyful and easy to follow, with prayer books with English to borrow, the Torah reading, a short talk and a children's program, then a hot Kiddush lunch for everyone. Visitors are offered honors like an aliyah to the Torah. First time? You will be warmly welcomed; just come.

shabbatText:
## Friday night: there is always a seat for you
Kabbalat Shabbat starts at {kabbalat-shabbat}, and then the Labkowski family sits down to Friday night dinner, and you are always welcome to join. Fresh challah, Kiddush over wine, songs around the table and good conversation that nobody is in a hurry to end. Come on your own, with your family or with a friend; your first time is as welcome as your fiftieth. Just let us know you are coming, with the “Come for a Shabbat meal” button or at 925-384-7242.

## Shabbat morning: services open to everyone
Saturday at 10 AM. Traditional prayers in a relaxed, friendly room, with a bilingual prayer book so you can follow along whether or not you read Hebrew. There is the Torah reading, a short talk, and children are part of it all. Come for the whole morning or for part of it; nobody is counting.

## Kiddush: come for the cholent
After services the whole community sits down together to a hot Kiddush lunch: a warm bowl of cholent, a l'chaim and plenty of time to talk. It is open to everyone, every Shabbat. Join us whenever you'd like.

## Mark an occasion with the community
A birthday, an anniversary or a yahrzeit? [Sponsor a Kiddush](/sponsor-a-kiddush) and the whole community celebrates or remembers with you.
